question.text: Paragraph: Let $V_r$ denotes the sum of the first $r$ terms of an arithmetic progression $(A P)$ whose first term is $r$ and the common difference is $(2 r-1)$. Let $T_r=V_{r+1}-V_r-2$ and $Q_r=T_{r+1}-T_r$ for $r=1,2, \ldots$Question: $T_r$ is always

solution.text:
$V_{r+1}-V_r=(r+1)^3-r^3-\frac{1}{2}\left[(r+1)^2-r^2\right]+\frac{1}{2}(1)$
$$
\begin{aligned}
& =3 r^2+2 r+1 \\
\therefore \quad T_r & =3 r^2+2 r-1=(r+1)(3 r-1)
\end{aligned}
$$
which is a composite number.
